about.text: Khoa, khoya, khowa or mawa is a soft cheese widely used in South Asian cuisine, encompassing India, Nepal, and Pakistan. It is made of either dried whole milk or milk thickened by heating in an open iron pan. It is lower in moisture than typical fresh cheeses such as ricotta. It is made from whole milk instead of whey.

facts.v: Soft, about 50 % moisture; base for sweets
Grainy, milk curdled with acid while simmering; for kalakand
Whole milk simmered for hours in a wide iron pan until about a fifth of its volume is left
About 5.5 % of India's milk goes into it, some 600,000 t a year
